conventions.convention: Finite FK laws retain distinct multigraph edge labels, count isolated components after boundary identification, and have weights p^|A|(1-p)^|E\A| q^kξ(A), with real q≥1 and 0<p<1.
Plane duality includes the unbounded face as one dual vertex and uses the identity partition on all dual face-vertices; dual-open labels complement primal-open labels, with p*/(1-p*)=q(1-p)/p.

Infinite-volume states are cylinder-probability limits of box laws extended by closed exterior edges. Free and wired states use identity and one-class boundary partitions; no equality at criticality is assumed.

Numerical cylinder limits and their threshold are distinguished from countably additive infinite-volume laws. Countable Choice is explicitly assumed for the latter extension and the subcritical coupling construction.
Torus cellulations retain all labelled loops and parallel edges for m=1,2; face boundaries retain occurrences before reduction modulo two.

Rotated crossing rectangles have closed sides. Auxiliary scales N are divisible by four; the surgery selects the first intersection along the vertical path, and only retained unqueried auxiliary labels must embed in the torus.
Cube influences use actual endpoint values on coordinate faces and elementary finite-box volumes; logarithms are natural.
Connectivity and annulus events use actual open edges, without artificial boundary-identification paths.
The Potts interaction is −J times the equal-color indicator. Its pinned order parameter subtracts 1/Q; the corresponding Ising interaction coupling satisfies J_P=2J_I.

load_bearing.statement: For finite multigraph FK laws with q≥1 and 0<p<1: log-supermodularity, positive association, spatial Markov conditioning, the stated single-edge conditional probabilities, and stochastic monotonicity in p and boundary wiring hold.

For real q≥1, at p=√q/(1+√q), closed rotated squares of scale N divisible by four have crossing probabilities at least a(q) when m>N; closed 3N/2-by-N rectangles have the stated crossing bound b(q)>0 when m>3N/2, including lattice-preserving translates.

For each q≥1 and α>1, there is c(α,q)>0 uniformly bounding below horizontal crossing probabilities of the ordinary vertex rectangle of width ceil(αn) and height n in every periodic square torus with m>ceil(αn), at p=√q/(1+√q).

For real q≥1, the numerical wired one-arm limit is positive above p_s=√q/(1+√q) and zero below it, without asserting its value at p_s or requiring Countable Choice. The statement additionally supplies finite annulus-product bounds, a Hamming-distance inequality, and subcritical one-arm bounds of every stated polynomial order.

For finite real q≥1, free and wired numerical cylinder limits exist, agree outside an at most countable parameter set, and satisfy Θ₁(p,q)≤Θ₀(p′,q) for 0<p<p′<1. The finite wired box-to-boundary probabilities converge to Θ₁(p,q).
For an increasing finite-box set C⊆[0,1]^n, n≥2, of elementary volume a, its maximum endpoint influence is at least a(1−a)log(n)/(4n).
For a finite FK law with q≥1, ε∈(0,1/2), p∈[ε,1−ε], |E|≥2, and an increasing event A with 0<φ(A)<1, max_e I_A(e)≥c(q,ε)φ(A)(1−φ(A))log|E|/|E|.

Given independent identically distributed shifted finite connected sets S_y containing their roots, with all positive size moments, their envelope M_z is almost surely finite and has a deterministic uniform average bound over all sufficiently large lattice animals containing 0.

Under Countable Choice, for every real q≥1 and 0<p<√q/(1+√q), wired cluster sizes have every positive moment, and all arbitrary-boundary cylinder-limit FK states satisfy a uniform exponential two-point connectivity bound.
